title: test(types): anchor the objectui#8466 calendar pin file to behaviour, not formatting
body:
Fixes #8832

The `objectui#8466` calendar pin file held four assertions whose truth depended on how text happened to be **written** rather than on what the code **does**. Each is re-anchored to the fact it names, and each new verdict is shown going red against a mutation of that fact.

⛔ The file is **not** rewritten. 4 of its 19 tests are touched; the compile-time `siblingPins` tuple is untouched and is still the real pin for the sibling interface; everything else stands. Test count is 19 before and 19 after.

## The four sites — addresses re-derived on `main`, not taken from the card

Every address in the card had drifted. These are my own readings of `packages/types/src/__tests__/calendar-flat-color-allday-8466.test.ts` at `main` = `16fc4cf20` (422 lines, 15 `it(` blocks, 19 tests):

| site | on `main` | was anchored to | now anchored to |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `:218` | the literal `(schema as any).KEY` **cast spelling** in the renderer source | a schema-read census over `getCalendarConfig`'s **own body**, sliced out by brace matching. It sees the bare `schema.KEY` and the cast form alike, so the verdict is *the renderer reads this key*, not *it reads it through a cast*. |
| 2 | `:230` | a regex over the `useMemo(...)` **dependency list's text** | the same census run over that dependency list, **sliced out by bracket matching** from a whitespace-tolerant locator. Order, wrapping and print width cannot reach the result; only the dependency itself can. |
| 3 | `:244` | the README's **line wrap**, `'at your own' + newline + 'fields when they differ.'` | the markdown **block** that teaches all five, with the block's internal whitespace collapsed. A blank line between blocks is structure; where lines break inside one is formatting. |
| 4 | the `it` at `:315`, assertions `:327` and `:328` | a record literal it had written three lines earlier, plus a tuple counted against a hard-coded `5` | the `it` is renamed to say it keeps the compile-time tuple referenced, and its one runtime assertion now checks that tuple's **arity against `FLAT_KEYS`** — a sixth flat key with no sixth slot goes red, which a shorter tuple type-checking silently would not. |

⚠️ Site 1 was the sharpest: dropping the `as any` cast is the cleanup that declaring these keys makes possible, so the pin went red on the improvement it existed to enable.

⚠️ The card describes site 4 as sitting at `:262-275`. On `main` that range is a substantive `safeParse` refusal test with two firing controls, not a vacuous assertion — the vacuous one is the `it` at `:315`. Confirmed independently; see the report on the card. One refinement: that `it` carried **two** vacuous runtime assertions, `:327` (the record literal the card names) and `:328` (`toHaveLength(5)`), and both are addressed.

The compile-time tuple stays at `:147` on `main` (`:167` on this branch) and is not deleted, weakened, or moved.

## Firing controls — one reading per site

Every mutation was applied to disk, proved landed by a blob-hash difference plus a single-line `grep -c`, run, then restored by `git checkout HEAD -- path` with the restore proved by `git diff HEAD` being **0 bytes** (never by an exit code). Final `git status --porcelain` was 0 bytes. The mutated artefacts are read by `readFileSync` at test time, so no build step sits between the mutation and the verdict.

| site | mutation of the behaviour it now names | reading |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `getCalendarConfig` stops reading `colorField` (`colorField: (schema as any).colorField,` becomes `colorField: undefined,`); the memo dependency list left intact | **RED** — `vitest exit=1`, `1 failed / 18 passed`, on `getCalendarConfig reads all five flat keys off the node`: *"getCalendarConfig no longer reads the flat colorField"*. Site 2 stayed green, so the two are independent. |
| 2 | `allDayField` is removed from the config memo's dependency list; the `getCalendarConfig` read left intact (probed: dep line 1 to 0, function read still 1) | **RED** — `vitest exit=1`, `1 failed / 18 passed`, on `...and allDayField is LOAD-BEARING`: *"allDayField left the config memo's dependency list"*. Site 1 stayed green. |
| 3 | `colorField` is moved out of the teaching paragraph into its own block — still present in the README (backticked count 2), so the per-key loop stays satisfied | **RED** — `vitest exit=1`, `1 failed / 18 passed`, on `the README still teaches all five together`: *"the five flat keys are no longer taught in one block: expected 0 to be greater than 0"*. |
| 4 | the `colorField` slot is deleted from the `siblingPins` tuple (type entry and value) | **RED** — `vitest exit=1`, `1 failed / 18 passed`: *"a flat key has no `siblingPins` slot, so the sibling interface is unpinned for it: expected [ true, true, true, true ] to have a length of 5 but got 4"*. |

## The other direction — each re-anchor survives the change that used to break it

A re-anchor that can no longer go red is a deleted test; a re-anchor that still reddens on formatting is not a fix. Both halves were measured.

| site | formatting change applied to disk | old assertion | new assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | the future cleanup: all **23** `(schema as any).` casts dropped to `schema.` | **would have failed** — re-evaluated against the cleaned file, `toContain('(schema as any).KEY')` is `False` for all five | **GREEN**, `vitest exit=0`, 19 passed |
| 2 | the memo call re-wrapped prettier-style across three lines and its 8 deps reversed | **would have failed** — the old regex re-evaluated against the reformatted file returns `False` | **GREEN**, `vitest exit=0`, 19 passed |
| 3 | the teaching paragraph re-wrapped onto one line | **would have failed** — `toContain('at your own' + newline + 'fields when they differ.')` is `False` | **GREEN**, `vitest exit=0`, 19 passed |

## Controls carried by the new assertions themselves

A control is only a control if it is known to fire in the region being tested, so each new verdict carries one from inside that region:

- **site 1** — `calendar` is read inside `getCalendarConfig` and is not one of the five (the slice is not empty by accident); `objectName` is read all over the same *file* and never inside that function (a slice that had swallowed the file fails here).
- **site 2** — `calendar` is in that very dependency list; `objectName` and `filter` are read elsewhere in the same file, `objectName` in the sibling `dataConfig` memo, and are deliberately out of this one.
- **site 3** — the same block search over the same README returns **0** blocks once `swatchField`, which the README does not teach, joins the key set.
- **the census instrument itself** — the existing reads-census `it` now asserts **one control per read form**: `schema.objectName` is read bare and `(schema as any).defaultView` through a cast. A single bare-form control would have left the cast form unmeasured, which is the half site 1 depends on.

## Verification

Head sha `0497a5f3a`. Commands and the exit code each printed, captured before any pipe.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/calendar-flat-color-allday-8466.test.ts` — exit **0**, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 19 passed (19)`. Same counts before the change.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` — exit **0**, `Test Files 173 passed (173)`, `Tests 3404 passed (3404)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` — exit **0** (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.examples.json && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`). Proof this covers the edited file rather than excluding it: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit --listFiles` lists 639 files, of which **1** is `calendar-flat-color-allday-8466.test.ts`.
- `pnpm exec eslint .` in `packages/types` — exit **0**, **243** files, 0 errors, 278 warnings; the edited file contributes exactly **2** `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` warnings, which is the count its own docblock claims, so that claim is not stale. No type-aware linting is configured in `eslint.config.js` (no `project` / `projectService` / `parserOptions`), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.
- Gates: `check:new-line-citations` exit **0** (`0 new citation(s)`), `check:control-bytes` exit **0**, `check:comment-mask-corpus` exit **0**, `check:unreferenced-sources` exit **0**, `check-changeset-presence` exit **0**, `check-changeset-no-major` exit **0**, `check-changeset-fixed` exit **0**, `check-changeset-overwrite` exit **0**.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on both changed paths: `NOT GOVERNED`. The PR stays draft regardless — landing is the seat's.
- Self-scan for control bytes over both changed files: `grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]'` exit **1** (no match).

Changeset: `.changeset/calendar-flat-key-pins-anchor-to-behaviour.md` with **empty frontmatter** — the gate's explicit declared-as-releasing-nothing path for a change confined to `src/__tests__/`.

## 验收备注

Out of scope for this card, noted and **not** filed — none is a reproducible bug, a declared-contract violation, or a metadata trap, and the card scoped itself to four assertions out of nineteen:

- Three further off-disk assertions in the same file are still literal-text anchors of the same family: the registration pins at `:311`/`:312` on `main` assert the exact call spelling `ComponentRegistry.register('object-calendar', ObjectCalendarRenderer`, and `:227` is a bare `toContain('allDayField')` over the whole renderer. They are not among the four the card names, and the card's opening credits the rest of the file, so they are left alone. Carrier: the next PR that touches this file, or a follow-up to this card if the seat wants the family closed rather than the four instances.
- `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` reads all five flat keys through `(schema as any)` even though both are now declared. Dropping those casts is the cleanup this card's pins were blocking; it is a `plugin-calendar` change, not a `packages/types` one. This PR measures that the cleanup now lands green (23 casts dropped, 19 tests still passing), but does not perform it. Carrier: whoever does the `plugin-calendar` cast cleanup.
